title: Add an action
description: Add a 1-second action at the playhead, see when Add Action is available, and find out why Frame Job might not place one.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Add Action puts a new [action](/motion/actions/) on the selected clip at the playhead, ready for you to say what it animates to.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
  keys="⌥⌘K"
  where="Clip tab ▸ action lane ▸ + (Add Action)"
  tools="add_action"
/>

## Add Action

<Steps>

1. Select a clip and put the playhead over it.

2. Press <kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>. **Clip ▸ Add Action** and the **+** button in the Clip tab's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) do the same.

3. In the Clip tab, change what you want the clip to reach by the end of the action. To fade the clip out over that second, for example, set **Opacity** in the **Picture** sub-tab to 0%.

</Steps>

The new action starts at the playhead, lasts 1 second and uses the **Linear** curve. It's one undo step.

## A new action starts empty

A new action's end state is empty, so it changes nothing until you edit it. The band appears, and the clip looks and sounds the same as before.

The action is selected as it's added, so the Clip tab is ready for its end state. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/). The playhead stays where it is, at the action's start, so the preview shows the change only once you move through the action or play it.

## When Add Action is available

Add Action needs the playhead over a selected clip. Otherwise **Clip ▸ Add Action** is greyed out, and the action lane's **+** button beeps.

## Several clips selected

With several clips selected, the action goes on the first selected clip under the playhead and isn't selected, because only a single selected clip can have a selected action. Select that clip alone to edit the new action.

## When there's no room for an action

The new action needs a clear second after the playhead. Frame Job beeps and adds nothing when the action would:

- overlap another action on the clip, or
- run past the clip's end.

The reason appears at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused:". See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).

Near the end of a clip, move the playhead back first, or [shorten an existing action](/motion/change-an-action/). A clip shorter than 1 second has no room for an action from Add Action.

## Other commands that make actions

These commands write ordinary actions. They show as bands and edit like any other.

---
title: "Animate a grade"
description: "Put a grade inside an action so it changes over time: what ramps, what switches at the end, how each control shows it, and how to take it back out."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Most grade settings can change over time. Put a change inside an [action](/motion/actions/) and a shot can warm up as the sun comes out, drain to black and white, or ease into a new contrast curve.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
  keys="⌥⌘K"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ action lane', 'Clip tab ▸ Color']}
  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_video']}
/>

## Grade inside an action

<Steps>

1. Select the clip and [add an action](/motion/add-an-action/), or [select one](/motion/select-an-action/) on its action lane.

2. Open the **Color** sub-tab.

3. Change a control. The change goes to the action's end state, and the value ramps there from where it stands when the action starts.

4. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to watch the grade travel.

</Steps>

Light, Color, Wheels, Curves and the look's **Amount** can all animate, and on an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) so can **Strength** and the [Qualifier](/color/qualifiers/).

While the action is selected, every control shows the value at the action's end. When you're done, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to go back to editing the clip itself. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for how an action's end state works in every tab.

:::tip
An adjustment clip can't take a transition. To fade a grade in, set its **Strength** to 0 % on the clip, then add an action and raise **Strength** to 100 %.
:::

## What ramps smoothly

These move gradually from the start value to the end value, along the action's curve:

- every slider in **Light** and **Color**
- each wheel's colour push and master in **Wheels**
- the look's **Amount**
- **Strength** on an adjustment clip
- the Qualifier's numbers: **Centre**, **Width**, **Soft**, **Low**, **High** and **Blur**

## Curves animate

Curves in an action always animate, on all six channels, including **Hue** and **Sat**. An edit to a curve goes to the action's end even when you add or delete a point.

| The two curves | How they animate |
| --- | --- |
| Same number of points | They ramp point by point |
| One is a straight line | The straight one lines up with the other curve's points, then they ramp point by point |
| Different numbers of points | Their values blend over the action, from the first curve's result to the second's |

### Animate a curve back to neutral

To have a curve straighten out over the action, write a straight curve to its end:

- For one channel, right-click its cell in the picker and choose **Reset Red**, or whichever channel it is. The item is greyed out while that channel is already straight.
- For every channel, right-click the plot and choose **Set end value to default**.

The section's **Reset** isn't there while an action is selected. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/).

## A look switches instead

content.content:
## `qualifier`

Narrows which pixels an adjustment clip's grade reaches, by hue, saturation and luma. It mirrors the Color sub-tab's **Qualifier** section. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).

The qualifier is for adjustment clips only. On any other clip it's an error naming the clip. It reads the picture behind the clip, before the grade.

`qualifier` is `{hue, saturation, luma, invert, blur}`.

| Key | Keys inside it | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hue` | `center`, `width`, `softness` | In degrees. `center` is 0 to 360 and wraps. `width` is 0 to 360, fully selected about the centre. `softness` is 0 to 180, the fall-off outside each edge. A colour's selection fades out as its chroma falls from 0.06 to 0.02, and at 0.02 or under it's never selected. |
| `saturation` | `low`, `high`, `softness` | Each 0 to 1, with `low` no more than `high`. Near-black reads as 0. |
| `luma` | `low`, `high`, `softness` | Each 0 to 1, with `low` no more than `high`. Rec. 709 luma, or BT.2020 luma in an HLG project. |
| `invert` | | `true` selects everything else. |
| `blur` | | 0 to 1, 0 being off. Softens the selection by a Gaussian of 24 × `blur` canvas pixels, never the matte. It draws nothing with no range on. |

A range merges: `{hue: {}}` turns hue on at centre 30, width 50, softness 25, and saturation and luma turn on at low 0, high 1, softness 0.1. A partial range keeps the rest, and `null` turns a range off. The selection is the product of the ranges that are on. A value outside its bounds is refused, never clamped.

In an action the numbers animate, the hue centre taking the short way round, so 350 to 10 passes 0. A range turned on or off, and `invert`, switch when the action ends.

`render_frame` with `selection` set to the adjustment clip's id draws what the qualifier selects, as [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) does. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

## Related
| [Duplicate](/editing/duplicate-clips/), [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) and [Paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/) | The presets are kept. |
| [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) | Presets are copied with the rest of the picture settings. |

A During movement restarts at each cut, because each piece is a clip of its own. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at the cuts.

## Good to know

- A preset moves the picture only. A Fade leaves the sound as it is, so use [audio fades](/audio/fades/) for that.
- A preset on a [nest](/editing/nests/) moves everything inside the nest together.
- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/) have the section and draw the marks, but there's no picture to move. Only a preset's fade has an effect, and it fades the clip's strength.
- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) blurs a preset's movement like any other.
- [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) works out its zoom without a During movement, and tells you so with "This clip has During motion — the zoom is solved without it".
- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) works on an upright picture, so it won't take a clip with Spin in any slot.
